name: 浏览器自动化
description: 给 agent 的浏览器工具:打开网页、读页面结构、点击、填表、滚动、截图、按目标自动导航;面板地址栏带收藏和历史;网页里划词弹出复合框(引用标签 + 问题输入框,翻译/解释/朗读/收藏,回车把问题连同引用发送到对话),翻译与解释由 agent 完成后回显在框内。整页翻译在工具栏一行完成;整页解释与整页分析把正文交给对话里的 agent,答案就在对话里。面板内嵌宿主浏览器引擎视图(地址栏归插件,引擎与登录态归宿主)。

tools.name: browser_show
tools.description: Answer inside the selection popup in the web page. This is the ONLY way to deliver a result the user is waiting for there: when they select page text and pick 翻译 / 解释, or type a question into the popup, it waits for this call — answer with it instead of replying only in the conversation. It works only while that popup is open; if it has closed, nothing is displayed, so write the answer in the conversation (the page has no other surface for content).

text.description: The content to show — the full translation or explanation, not a summary of it.

title.description: Short heading for the result, e.g. "译文" or "要点". Optional.

kind.description: What this is: "translate" or "explain" when answering a selection-popup request, "chat" for a question the user typed into the popup — so the result is labelled correctly.

tools.name: browser_clips_list
tools.description: List the pieces of page text the user kept with the selection popup's 收藏 button. Use it when they ask what they saved while reading, or refer to "我收藏的那段话".

query.description: Words to match against the saved text and the page it came from. Empty returns the most recent clips.

tools.name: browser_history_search
tools.description: Search the pages this browser has visited. Use it when the user refers to a site they (or you) opened before — "再打开上次那个网站" — instead of asking them to retype the address. Returns each match's title, URL, when it was last visited, and how often.

query.description: Words to match against page titles and URLs, e.g. "招聘" or "github react" — every word must appear. Empty returns the most recent visits.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: browser_recipes
tools.description: List recorded shortcut operations (recipes) for this SITE (registrable domain, so subdomains are included): the steps, what each step was expected to do, how often it ran, when it last worked, and — after a failed run — which step broke and why. After navigating to a site that mentions saved operations, read them here and run the steps with browser_act.

origin.description: Only show recipes for this origin or site, e.g. https://search.bilibili.com or bilibili.com

tools.name: browser_recipe_delete
tools.description: Delete a recorded recipe by name or id — when the user asks to remove it, or it is marked stale.

name.description: Recipe name as shown by browser_recipes

tools.name: browser_favorites_list
tools.description: List the sites the user starred in the browser panel. Use it to resolve "打开我常用的那个网站" into a real URL, or to see which sites the user cares about before navigating. A site with notes shows its memory count.

tools.name: browser_site_memory
tools.description: Read or edit the user's long-term memory for a site: what the site is for, where things live, what to avoid. The user writes these in the browser panel; browser_navigate already injects them for favorited sites. Use action "list" to read them before complex work. Action "add" stores ONE sentence when the user asks you to remember something, or when a finished multi-step run on a favorited site taught you a verifiable fact — it is created as PENDING and only becomes confirmed knowledge when the user approves it in the panel; unconfirmed notes are injected with an explicit (AI 观察，未确认) label. If the page contradicts a note, use action "dispute" with that note's id and a reason: the note is paused as 可疑 and the user decides; do not edit or delete around it. You may update / remove only your own unconfirmed notes: a note the user confirmed is theirs, and editing it is refused. Never write memory on your own initiative beyond that, and never treat memory as live page state: the page wins, and you tell the user which note is wrong.

action.description: list (default) reads the notes; add / update / dispute / remove act on them.

text.description: The one sentence to store (add), or the replacement text (update).

reason.description: dispute only: how the page contradicts the note, in one sentence.

enabled.description: false pauses a note so it is no longer injected; true resumes it.

url.description: The page or site to read/write; defaults to the current page.

tools.name: browser_workflow
tools.description: The user's saved routines that span sites (export here, import there). A workflow is a readable checklist of steps, each optionally naming a site and a saved recipe; it is NOT executable code and never bypasses a page's login or confirmation. Use action "list" when the user refers to a recurring routine ("按每周订单同步走") or asks what routines exist. Use "add" / "update" / "remove" only when the user asks you to remember or change one, and "mark" after running one to record the outcome. Every workflow is visible and editable in the memory center.

action.description: list (default) reads; add / update / remove change the routines; mark records a run's outcome.

id.description: Workflow id from list (update / remove / mark).

name.description: The routine's name, e.g. "每周订单同步" (add / update).

steps.description: For add / update: the routine in order, one short sentence per step.

text.description: What to do in this step.

site.description: Origin or domain this step happens on, e.g. admin.shopify.com.

recipe.description: Optional saved recipe name to use on that site.

ok.description: mark only: whether the run succeeded.

error.description: mark only: what failed, when ok is false.

tools.name: browser_collect
tools.description: Run a saved deterministic reading recipe (a collection): open a fixed URL, extract named fields from a list, and optionally open the first few items to extract detail fields. Returns ONLY the stored fields as compact data — never a page snapshot — so recurring reads cost almost nothing and need no re-analysis. The URL may contain {{name}} placeholders; pass values on run so one recipe works for every keyword. Use it for stable, structured pages read repeatedly (a trending list, a dashboard, a table). Create one only after verifying selectors on the live page with browser_evaluate, and run it once after adding to prove it works. Health: two failed runs mark it stale; fix with update or remove it. Read-only: it navigates and extracts, never clicks or submits.

action.description: list (default) reads the saved recipes; add / update / remove manage them; run executes one and returns its data.

id.description: Collection id from list (update / remove / run).

values.description: For run: fills the {{name}} placeholders in the collection URL, e.g. {"关键词":"AI"}. Missing values are reported, not guessed.

name.description: A short name, e.g. "每日趋势" (add / update).

url.description: The page the run opens first (add / update). May contain {{name}} placeholders, e.g. "https://site/search?q={{关键词}}".

list.description: How to read the list page.

scope.description: CSS selector for one row; empty means one record from the whole page.

fields.description: Fields to extract from each row.

selector.description: CSS within the row; empty means the row itself.

limit.description: Rows to return at most (1–50, default 20).

detail.description: Optional: open the first few rows and read fields on each page.

urlField.description: Which list field holds the item URL, e.g. "link".

fields.description: Fields to extract on each opened page.

waitFor.description: Selector to wait for before extracting (for lazily rendered pages).

count.description: How many of the first rows to open (1–5, default 3).

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the built-in browser to a URL and wait for it to load. Returns the final URL and page title. If the page is a human-verification challenge or a login form, the result says so: those are the USER's to complete — do not click, fill, or try to bypass them; tell the user to act in the browser panel and continue when they say so.

url.description: The URL to open, e.g. https://example.com

tools.name: browser_tab_list
tools.description: List this conversation's browser tabs: id, title/url, and which is focused. Multi-tab workflows start here.

tools.name: browser_tab_open
tools.description: Open a NEW browser tab (optionally at a URL) in this conversation and focus it. The page tools then act on the focused tab, or on `tab` when given. Page state (login, scroll, forms) is kept per tab.

url.description: URL to load; omit for a blank tab.

tools.name: browser_tab_switch
tools.description: Focus one of this conversation's tabs by id (from browser_tab_list). Subsequent page tools act on it.

tools.name: browser_tab_close
tools.description: Close one of this conversation's tabs by id.

tools.name: browser_get_state
tools.description: Get the current URL, page title, and a snapshot of the page's interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs — each with a ref you can pass to browser_click / browser_fill). Call this FIRST after navigating to see what is on the page. Do NOT call it again just to confirm an action: every action (and browser_act) already returns a fresh snapshot. Use browser_screenshot only for visual layout.

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Find interactive elements on the current page by text query (fuzzy match, scored). Returns matches with role, visible text, page section, and a ref usable as a click/fill selector. Use it when browser_get_state's snapshot was truncated or you need to locate one specific control.

query.description: Text to search for, e.g. "登录" or "search"

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element in the built-in browser. Waits up to 5s for the element, scrolls it into view, then clicks. The result reports what changed on the page (new text or a URL change), so you do NOT need to re-check with browser_get_state or browser_evaluate. On failure the result suggests similar elements. If the click opens a confirm(), the answer depends on the session permission mode: DISMISSED in 默认 (the user approves risky steps one by one), ACCEPTED in 完全访问 (the user already delegated the session). The result always reports what the dialog asked and what was chosen; pass dialog to override.

selector.description: Element selector. Preferred: a ref from browser_get_state/browser_find, e.g. "[12]". Also accepted: text="登录", role=button[name="提交"], or a CSS selector.

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

dialog.description: How to answer a confirm()/alert() raised by this click. Omit it to follow the session permission mode (默认 → dismiss, 完全访问 → accept). Pass accept/dismiss only to override that.

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Run several browser steps in one call: click / fill / select / upload / hover / wait. Steps run in order and stop at the first failure; the result lists what each step did plus the page's CURRENT interactive snapshot — that snapshot is authoritative, so do NOT follow up with browser_get_state or browser_evaluate to confirm. Use it for sequences you can already see on the page (fill every field, then submit). Do NOT batch a step whose target only appears after an earlier one — click that first, look, then batch the rest. A click that raises a confirm() follows the session permission mode (默认 → dismiss, 完全访问 → accept). On a favorited site a fully successful batch is saved as a recipe automatically; pass a short name for it. If you are following a saved recipe, pass recipe:"<name>" so its health is tracked.

steps.description: Ordered steps; each step uses exactly one key.

click.description: Selector to click — a ref like "[3]" is preferred

dialog.description: Answer a confirm()/alert() raised by this step. Omit to follow the session permission mode (默认 → dismiss, 完全访问 → accept).

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

name.description: Short name for the recipe recorded after a successful batch on a favorited site (e.g. "搜索视频"). Omit to let it be named after the page.

recipe.description: When these steps come from a saved recipe, pass its name here: a success refreshes the recipe, a failure counts toward retiring it.

tools.name: browser_upload
tools.description: Attach local files to a page's upload control — file pickers, '添加附件', '上传' buttons, and drag-and-drop-only zones (pages with no file input at all: the host synthesises a real drop). Clicking the control lets the browser report which input the page wants, so hidden, dynamically created and iframe-hosted (same-origin or cross-origin) inputs all work. Pass absolute paths. NEVER call browser_fill on a file input, and do NOT read file bytes yourself — this tool already does. The result reports what appeared on the page, so do NOT verify with browser_evaluate.

selector.description: The control that opens the file picker — a ref like "[12]" is preferred — or the file input itself.

files.description: Absolute paths of the files to attach.

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_fill
tools.description: Fill an input field (replaces existing content; works with React/Vue controlled inputs). Focuses the field first and reads it back afterwards: the result reports the field's current value, so do NOT verify it yourself with browser_evaluate.

selector.description: Input selector — same formats as browser_click (ref like "[3]" is preferred).

value.description: The text to type into the field

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Hover the pointer over an element — for menus and tooltips that only appear on hover.

selector.description: Element selector — same formats as browser_click.

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_select
tools.description: Select an option in a <select> dropdown by value or visible text. The result reports which option ended up selected — no need to read it back.

selector.description: Select-element selector — same formats as browser_click.

value.description: Option value or visible text to select

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page up or down.

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Run a JavaScript expression in the page context and return its JSON value. Power tool for reading computed data (e.g. document.title, table contents) that the snapshot misses. The page can tell it runs — never use it to bypass a site's defenses.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate, e.g. JSON.stringify({h1: document.querySelector('h1')?.textContent})

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.

tools.name: browser_walk
tools.description: Goal-directed navigation: state the target (e.g. "进入个人设置页") and the browser plans and executes the click path itself, using screenshot analysis. Use it when a site needs several dependent clicks to reach a place and you do not know its structure. Requires a vision model to be configured; falls back to keyword matching when planning fails. Verify the result with browser_get_state afterwards.

goal.description: The destination in plain language, e.g. "打开文章编辑器"

maxSteps.description: Maximum click steps to try. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page in the built-in browser. Returns a base64 PNG image you can see directly. Use it for visual layout, design, charts, or CAPTCHA-style content the element snapshot cannot express — NOT to confirm form values, text, or whether a click worked; the snapshot returned by the action already answers those.

fullPage.description: Capture the full scrollable page instead of the viewport

tab.description: Act on this tab id (from browser_tab_list) instead of the conversation's focused tab.
